author: justinvdm
body:
## Context
We have two vite environments: `client` (for client side) and `worker` (for code run in cloudflare worker).

The build step of `worker` relies on the build manifest vite generates for `client` - this asset includes mappings from the entry point source paths to their corresponding built destination paths.

It relies on the manifest so that we can replace references to client entry points in jsx (e.g. in `Document.tsx`) with their corresponding built assets.

## Problem
We read the client manifest from disk the first time, then hold onto it in memory and use the in memory value instead for subsequent attempts to read it. However, when reading the client manifest, we do not check whether the current context is the `worker` environment (not the `client` environment). This causes two issues:
* if this is the first build/release for the project on your machine, there won't be a manifest yet by the time we read => we'll default to an empty lookup for it (`{}`)
* if you had released before with different code, the new manifest hasn't been generated yet by the time we read => we'll use an outdated manifest
  * Seen here
     * #378 
     * #399

## Solution
* Change the plugin that relies on the manifest to only run for the `worker` environment (it should not be running for `client` anyways).
* We also now throw rather than default to `{}` so that we can catch issues if for some reason we are still needing the manifest before it exists

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>prometheus/client_golang (github.com/prometheus/client_golang)</summary>

### [`v1.22.0`](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/releases/tag/v1.22.0): - 2025-04-07

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/compare/v1.21.1...v1.22.0)

:warning: This release contains potential breaking change if you use experimental `zstd` support introduce in [#​1496](https://redirect.github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/1496) :warning:

Experimental support for `zstd` on scrape was added, controlled by the request `Accept-Encoding` header.
It was enabled by default since version 1.20, but now you need to add a blank import to enable it.
The decision to make it opt-in by default was originally made because the Go standard library was expected to have default zstd support added soon,
[https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62513](https://redirect.github.com/golang/go/issues/62513) however, the work took longer than anticipated and it will be postponed to upcoming major Go versions.

e.g.:

> ```go
> import (
>   _ "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp/zstd"
> )
> ```

author: 2547techno
body:
Currently, the use of `c2.HTTPRequest.create(...)` in typescript results in code that produces the following error after being compiled with TSTL:
```
Failed to evaluate command from plugin HTTP Error: stack index 1, expected number, received table: (bad argument into 'std::shared_ptr<chatterino::lua::api::HTTPRequest>(sol::this_state, enum chatterino::NetworkRequestType, QString)')
```

This is because the generated lua code for this function call is:
```lua
c2.HTTPRequest:create(...)
```
This PR updates the types file so that the generated lua code is:
```lua
c2.HTTPRequest.create(...)
```

author: danwritecode
body:
## Description

This PR introduces **prompt deletion** functionality and unifies the OpenAI-compatible completions API endpoint for both streaming and non-streaming requests.

---

### Backend

- **Prompt Deletion**
  - Adds a transactional, multi-step deletion process in `PromptRepository::delete_prompt` to ensure all related data (prompt versions, tool associations, evals, eval runs, and logs) is cleaned up.
  - Handles circular references by nulling `current_prompt_version_id` before deletion.
  - Controller now logs actions and removes the prompt from cache after deletion.

- **Completions API**
  - Unifies `/chat/completions` endpoint to handle both streaming and non-streaming requests via a single endpoint, using the `stream` flag in the payload.
  - Removes all `/stream` endpoints from the router.
  - Introduces a `CompletionResponse` enum for ergonomic Axum response handling.

---

### Frontend

- **Prompt Deletion**
  - Adds a "Delete" button to the prompt edit dialog, styled as a "danger" button.
  - Prompts for confirmation before deletion.
  - Updates the local prompt list and UI after deletion.
  - Adds robust error handling and logging.

- **Completions API**
  - All calls to `/execute/chat` and `/execute/chat/stream` are replaced with the unified `/execute` endpoint, with `stream: true/false` in the payload.
  - SSE connections now use the unified endpoint.

- **Styling**
  - Adds a new `danger` button type to `primary-button.vue` for destructive actions.

---

### Other

- Adds useful logs for debugging prompt deletion.
- Improves error handling and user feedback throughout.

---

body:
# Description

This PR introduces a commit message linter hook to enforce the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) standard.

### Changes:
- Added `commit-message-linter` to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
- Ensures all commit messages follow the `type(scope): description` format
- Validates commit messages using `--type conventional`

### Why:
Maintaining consistent and structured commit messages helps with:
- automated changelog generation,
- clean Git history,
- better code reviews and CI integrations.

### Usage:
Ensure the hook is activated:
```bash
pre-commit install --hook-type commit-msg
```

All commit messages will now be validated automatically before completing the commit.

author: gcruces95
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the `cars` module, including the use of UUIDs for car IDs, the addition of DTOs for input validation, and the implementation of global validation pipes. These changes improve the robustness, maintainability, and security of the application.

### Input Validation and DTOs
* Added `CreateCarDto` and `UpdateCarDto` classes with validation rules using `class-validator` to enforce input constraints (`src/cars/dto/create-car.dto.ts`, `src/cars/dto/update-car.dto.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-49762e9a3cf17b5117aa4ee71075c218103d8fff0ed80f2b514d5b74bce10751R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ba196a40ee8f515f9543b9e72bd69ee0faf2b6b458372d7274644d3ac3bf2211R1-R21).
* Updated the `CarsController` methods to use DTOs for request payloads and replaced `ParseIntPipe` with `ParseUUIDPipe` for ID validation (`src/cars/cars.controller.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3e81f38f526872fb0f7c6465a6a9935a1f6bf6a368bd71546737b39fc963de0bL1-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3e81f38f526872fb0f7c6465a6a9935a1f6bf6a368bd71546737b39fc963de0bL19-R36).

### Global Validation
* Configured a global `ValidationPipe` in the main application to enforce input validation across all controllers. This includes options to whitelist valid properties and forbid non-whitelisted properties (`src/main.ts`).

### Transition to UUIDs
* Updated the `Car` interface to use UUIDs for `id` and replaced numeric IDs with UUIDs in the `CarsService` and its methods (`src/cars/cars.service.ts`, `src/cars/interfaces/car.interface.ts`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3309a3a9d60e9664ac081251f0c08a2ca104726aeffa82b46cc444589cf4cdaaL1-R62) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2aa91e8160cc59feb847a834a12f3429c2f0a2eb36db4ef0537e35c1baea0dfbR1-R8).

### Dependency Updates
* Added `class-transformer`, `class-validator`, and `uuid` to the project dependencies in `package.json` to support DTO validation and UUID generation (`package.json`).

body:
Couple major changes here:

- Remove redundant chainId check - this is already done in sendTransactionInternal so we don't need to do it twice
- Parallelize calls to fetch nonce and zkEstimateFee. Fee estimation doesn't seem to rely on the nonce, so we can do these calls in parallel, which will shave off ~100-200 ms

In the future we can shave off even more time by optimistically assuming all wallets are deployed, but that'll require larger fixes to the tests.

This PR focuses on optimizing the `prepareTransactionRequest` function in the `agw-client` package by parallelizing asynchronous calls, which improves performance and efficiency during transaction preparation.

- Added parallelization for async calls in `prepareTransactionRequest`.
- Removed the `chainId` from transaction requests.

author: csmangum
body:
This pull request introduces several significant updates to the `TelephonyRealtimeBridge` system, including improvements to session handling, logging, and testing, as well as the addition of a validation script to verify message flow sequences. The changes enhance error handling, streamline session initialization, and improve test coverage.

### Enhancements to session handling and logging:
* Refactored session initialization to delay sending `session.accepted` until after receiving the `SessionCreatedEvent`, ensuring proper synchronization between the telephony client and OpenAI Realtime API. A new flag, `waiting_for_session_creation`, was added to track this state (`fastagent/telephony_realtime_bridge.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-943152c177b2539ca798174d9f9fe70b2bbd8c37e1fc3af8e61fa5b96d41dfefL161-R175) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-943152c177b2539ca798174d9f9fe70b2bbd8c37e1fc3af8e61fa5b96d41dfefR270-R307)
* Improved error logging in `receive_from_realtime` to include detailed error codes, messages, and additional debugging information (`fastagent/telephony_realtime_bridge.py`).

### Configuration updates:
* Updated the session configuration to use `near_field` for `input_audio_noise_reduction` and `whisper-1` for `input_audio_transcription`, aligning with the latest OpenAI API capabilities (`fastagent/telephony_realtime_bridge.py`).

### Testing improvements:
* Enhanced the test suite for `TelephonyRealtimeBridge` by simulating the `SessionCreatedEvent` and verifying the delayed sending of `session.accepted`. This ensures the new session handling logic is properly validated (`tests/bot/test_telephony_realtime_bridge.py`).
* Removed unused imports in the test file, improving code cleanliness (`tests/bot/test_telephony_realtime_bridge.py`).

### New validation script:
* Added a comprehensive validation script, `validate_session_flow.py`, to test key message flow sequences, including session initialization and audio streaming. This script provides detailed feedback on the system's behavior and ensures compliance with expected workflows (`validation_scripts/validate_session_flow.py`).

### Description

This branch introduces the ability to favourite documents when the Studio rendering context provides Comlink.

- The favourite/unfavourite button is only rendered if Comlink is available.
- The favourite/unfavourite button is rendered in read-only mode while the initial state is fetched from the remote.
-  The favourite/unfavourite button is rendered in read-only mode for newly created documents that have not yet been created in Content Lake.
- Mutations are applied optimistically to local state. If the local value differs from the last known local value after a debounce period of 750ms, the local value is written to the remote. 

[Demo video](https://supercut.video/share/ash/hN1cSF9Ssr_0m5MEh1Z4iu)

#### Error handling

Note: the local state is not rolled back or synced when a write error occurs. This means it's possible for the local state to get out of sync with the remote. This will be resolved after the user reloads.

There are two primary scenarios that could occur:

1. An error occurs on write.
2. The user favourites the document elsewhere (e.g. another browser tab) after the initial state has been fetched.

As we intend to replace this implementation with the SDK, I'm not sure that it's worthwhile addressing right now.

### What to review

- The favourite/unfavourite functionality works correctly when Studio is rendered inside Dashboard.
- The favourite/unfavourite functionality does not appear when Studio is not rendered inside Dashboard.

### Testing

- Tested in Dashboard.
- Unit tests to follow.

body:
fixed #213

### 概要
tokenizerが元々`"a""b"`を`["a","b"]`別トークンで扱っていたのを`["\"a\"\b\""]`という形で一つのトークンにまとめる形にしました。

クオートをなくす処理についてはParserの責務ですので、このプルリクエストでは対応していません。
詳しくはｰ>#200

### 確認方法
`make`後`./minish`で確認で動作可能ですが、効果を確認するのは難しいです。
一応対応前後でechoの挙動が変わります。
- 修正前: `echo "a""b" -> "a" "b"` ※token区切りでスペースを入れて出力しているため、修正前はスペースが入る
- 修正後: `echo "a""b" -> "a""b"`

author: chusitooxduwu
body:
This pull request introduces several changes, including the addition of a new utility for tracking loading times, refactoring of ViewModel classes for better organization, and minor updates to improve code maintainability. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### New Feature: Loading Time Tracking

* Added `LoadingTimeTracker` utility in `app/src/main/java/com/example/sporthub/utils/LoadingTimeTracker.kt` to measure and log screen load times, with integration for Firebase Firestore to store analytics data. This includes methods to start tracking, stop tracking, and update average load times.
* Integrated `LoadingTimeTracker` into `HomeFragment` to track and record loading times for the "Home View" screen. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aa5e7381b9777cd5e8bbf6be0895b579a791554a6b43caecaa3c03f1ce4a14c8R42-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aa5e7381b9777cd5e8bbf6be0895b579a791554a6b43caecaa3c03f1ce4a14c8R116-R117)

### Refactoring: ViewModel Reorganization

* Renamed `FindVenuesViewModel` from `app/src/main/java/com/example/sporthub/ui/findVenues/FindVenuesViewModel.kt` to `app/src/main/java/com/example/sporthub/viewmodel/FindVenuesViewModel.kt` and updated its package to `com.example.sporthub.viewmodel`.
* Renamed `VenueDetailViewModel` from `app/src/main/java/com/example/sporthub/ui/venueDetail/VenueDetailViewModel.kt` to `app/src/main/java/com/example/sporthub/viewmodel/VenueDetailViewModel.kt` and updated its package to `com.example.sporthub.viewmodel`.

### Enhancements in ViewModel Logic

* Updated `FindVenuesViewModel` to use `HashMap` instead of `mutableMapOf` for `venueCache` to align with standard practices.
* Added a new method `filterUpcomingBookings` in `VenueDetailViewModel` to filter bookings based on availability and start time, improving data handling logic.
* Integrated `filterUpcomingBookings` into the logic for processing bookings in `VenueDetailViewModel`.

### Codebase Cleanup

* Removed unused imports across multiple files, such as `SportsAdapter` and `Glide` in `FindVenuesFragment`, and `Observer` in `VenueListFragment`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0507ad5db6ec543e96a3b1d045e3cf2d76fb4a1d042a787af785e442b5f81155L19-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f16da35b39b4a9465d2400c64939b7640411a2a371dd3818ff4ef40550ee1afbL18-R23)
* Updated imports in affected files to reflect the new ViewModel package structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9725e65325c5e171b0e8f533cf2dd2a18a00692309241c8b13c599c04051aa55L16-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-54b1c7dd6d706b6a326027f643e8adc33ad73234b9af634cb89cda32e7f43669R11)

These changes enhance the maintainability and functionality of the codebase, particularly by introducing a robust mechanism for tracking loading performance and improving ViewModel organization.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v10.19.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10190)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.18.3...v10.19.0)

##### Minor Changes

- You can now allow specific versions of dependencies to run postinstall scripts. `onlyBuiltDependencies` now accepts package names with lists of trusted versions. For example:

  ```yaml
  onlyBuiltDependencies:
    - nx@21.6.4 || 21.6.5
    - esbuild@0.25.1
  ```

  Related PR: [#​10104](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/10104).

- Added support for exact versions in `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` [#​9985](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9985).

  You can now list one or more specific versions that pnpm should allow to install, even if those versions don’t satisfy the maturity requirement set by `minimumReleaseAge`. For example:

  ```yaml
  minimumReleaseAge: 1440
  minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
    - nx@21.6.5
    - webpack@4.47.0 || 5.102.1
  ```

### [`v10.18.3`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10183)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.18.2...v10.18.3)

##### Patch Changes

- Fix a bug where pnpm would infinitely recurse when using `verifyDepsBeforeInstall: install` and pre/post install scripts that called other pnpm scripts [#​10060](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10060).
- Fixed scoped registry keys (e.g., `@scope:registry`) being parsed as property paths in `pnpm config get` when `--location=project` is used [#​9362](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9362).
- Remove pnpm-specific CLI options before passing to npm publish to prevent "Unknown cli config" warnings [#​9646](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9646).
- Fixed EISDIR error when bin field points to a directory [#​9441](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9441).
- Preserve version and hasBin for variations packages [#​10022](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10022).
- Fixed `pnpm config set --location=project` incorrectly handling keys with slashes (auth tokens, registry settings) [#​9884](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9884).
- When both `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `.npmrc` exist, `pnpm config set --location=project` now writes to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (matching read priority) [#​10072](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10072).
- Prevent a table width error in `pnpm outdated --long` [#​10040](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10040).
- Sync bin links after injected dependencies are updated by build scripts. This ensures that binaries created during build processes are properly linked and accessible to consuming projects [#​10057](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10057).

### [`v10.18.2`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10182)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.18.1...v10.18.2)

##### Patch Changes

- `pnpm outdated --long` should work [#​10040](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10040).
- Replace ndjson with split2. Reduce the bundle size of pnpm CLI [#​10054](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/10054).
- `pnpm dlx` should request the full metadata of packages, when `minimumReleaseAge` is set [#​9963](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9963).
- pnpm version switching should work when the pnpm home directory is in a symlinked directory [#​9715](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9715).
- Fix `EPIPE` errors when piping output to other commands [#​10027](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10027).

### [`v10.18.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10181)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.18.0...v10.18.1)

##### Patch Changes

- Don't print a warning, when `--lockfile-only` is used [#​8320](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8320).
- `pnpm setup` creates a command shim to the pnpm executable. This is needed to be able to run `pnpm self-update` on Windows [#​5700](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/5700).
- When using pnpm catalogs and running a normal `pnpm install`, pnpm produced false positive warnings for "*skip adding to the default catalog because it already exists*". This warning now only prints when using `pnpm add --save-catalog` as originally intended.

### [`v10.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10180)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.17.1...v10.18.0)

##### Minor Changes

- Added network performance monitoring to pnpm by implementing warnings for slow network requests, including both metadata fetches and tarball downloads.

  Added configuration options for warning thresholds: `fetchWarnTimeoutMs` and `fetchMinSpeedKiBps`.
  Warning messages are displayed when requests exceed time thresholds or fall below speed minimums

  Related PR: [#​10025](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/10025).

##### Patch Changes

- Retry filesystem operations on EAGAIN errors [#​9959](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9959).
- Outdated command respects `minimumReleaseAge` configuration [#​10030](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/10030).
- Correctly apply the `cleanupUnusedCatalogs` configuration when removing dependent packages.
- Don't fail with a meaningless error when `scriptShell` is set to `false` [#​8748](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/8748).
- `pnpm dlx` should not fail when `minimumReleaseAge` is set [#​10037](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/10037).

### [`v10.17.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10171)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.17.0...v10.17.1)

##### Patch Changes

- When a version specifier cannot be resolved because the versions don't satisfy the `minimumReleaseAge` setting, print this information out in the error message [#​9974](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9974).
- Fix `state.json` creation path when executing `pnpm patch` in a workspace project [#​9733](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9733).
- When `minimumReleaseAge` is set and the `latest` tag is not mature enough, prefer a non-deprecated version as the new `latest` [#​9987](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9987).

### [`v10.17.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/HEAD/pnpm/CHANGELOG.md#10170)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v10.16.1...v10.17.0)

##### Minor Changes

- The `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` setting now supports patterns. For instance:

  ```yaml
  minimumReleaseAge: 1440
  minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
    - "@​eslint/*"
  ```

  Related PR: [#​9984](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/9984).

##### Patch Changes

- Don't ignore the `minimumReleaseAge` check, when the package is requested by exact version and the packument is loaded from cache [#​9978](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9978).
- When `minimumReleaseAge` is set and the active version under a dist-tag is not mature enough, do not downgrade to a prerelease version in case the original version wasn't a prereleas

author: robbieneko
body:
## Purpose of change (The Why)

As raised by Kheir and a few other members of the community, wholesale banning Brawlers from casting spells is perhaps a bit overkill.

While my initial stance was that those who opposed it and wanted to let spells through should code in the exceptions, I realized that this was a far better solution and one that I'd end up likely needing in some capacity in the future.

I'm somewhat surprised I didn't think of this initially.

## Describe the solution (The How)

- Adds a new spell flag, `"BRAWL"`
- Changes the check that prevents Brawlers from casting spells to instead also check for the spell flag, and let it through if it's detected
- Keeps a wholesale "You can't cast any of your spells because you're a brawler!" style of message around for the sake of it.
- Adds a debug spell for testing reasons

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Do it via an actual entry in the spells

That's how I did it originally, but I realized it was a bit silly when we have spell flags right there for simple booleans

- Add it to the can_cast_spells check instead of a new one for the "Can't cast any spells" style message

Just didn't feel right, and I felt that it should print out a unique message to make the cause clear.

## Testing

- Compiled
- Loaded in
- Tested while none of my known spells were able to be cast by brawlers, confirmed that it displayed the correct message
- Tested casting a non-brawler appropriate spell when I had a brawler appropriate spell, similarly displays correct message
- Tested the brawler-acceptable spell, it works just fine

## Additional context

I'm not adding it to spells in MN myself yet, though either I'll PR it later or someone else interested can.

Not added to docs yet because Scarf still hasn't finished migrating them and I don't want to make merge conflicts for him.

## Checklist

### Mandatory

- [x] I wrote the PR title in [conventional commit format](https://docs.cataclysmbn.org/en/contribute/changelog_guidelines/).
- [x] I ran the [code formatter](https://docs.cataclysmbn.org/en/contribute/contributing/#code-style).
- [x] I linked any relevant issues using [github keyword syntax](https://docs.cataclysmbn.org/en/contribute/contributing/#pull-request-notes) like `closes #1234` in [Summary of the PR](#purpose-of-change-the-why) so it can be closed automatically.
- [x] I've [committed my changes to new branch that isn't `main`](https://docs.cataclysmbn.org/en/contribute/contributing/#make-your-changes) so it won't cause conflict when updating `main` branch later.

### Optional

##### 🧪 Experiments Completed

The [stacks](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/reference/experiments/#stacks) experiment is now complete.

If you were previously using the flag `--experiment stacks` to opt in to experimental functionality, you no longer have to do so. Note that if you are, you will simply get a warning that it is no longer necessary.

##### 🛠️ Breaking Changes

Legacy commands (as replaced by the [CLI Redesign](https://redirect.github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/issues/3445) are now deprecated, and will be phased out at a future date, which will be scheduled in [#​3535](https://redirect.github.com/gruntwork-io/terragrunt/issues/3535). Make sure to subscribe to the issue if you would like to be informed when these deprecated features are no longer supported.

For instructions on migrating to the new commands provided after the CLI Redesign, read the [CLI Redesign Migration Guide](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/migrate/cli-redesign/).

The following are now deprecated:

-   `hclfmt` (use `hcl fmt` instead)
-   `hclvalidate` (use `hcl validate` instead)
-   `validate-inputs` (use `hcl validate --inputs` and `hcl validate --inputs --strict` instead)
-   `terragrunt-info` (use `info print` instead)
-   `output-module-groups` (use `find --dag --json` instead)
-   `render-json` (use `render --json -w` instead)
-   `graph-dependencies` (use `dag graph` instead)
-   `run-all` (use `run --all` instead)
-   `graph` (use `run --graph` instead)
-   The default command. e.g. `terragrunt workspace list` (use `terragrunt run -- workspace list` instead)
-   Default bootstrap (automatically provisioning backend resources without additional flags). This is now opt in behavior, and requires usage of the `--backend-bootstrap` flag or explicitly running the new `backend bootstrap` command.
-   `aws-provider-patch` (we are simply deprecating this command, and removing it when the other commands are removed. It served its purpose as a short term stopgap tool).

Note that this will not result in an immediate breaking change for users, as we’ll have an initial deprecation window to give users time to adjust to these changes. If you’d like to ensure that you are prepared for the future removal of legacy commands, you can take advantage of the [cli-redesign](https://terragrunt.gruntwork.io/docs/reference/strict-mode/#cli-redesign) strict control to opt in to the future breaking change early.

##### 💪🏽  Enhancements

The logging for stack generation has been improved to make it easier to determine at a glance the stack file that’s generating a particular unit.

author: dlund1010
body:
Implemented the ability to add friends. Behind the scenes this uses a new friend requests database that tracks who a request was sent from, who it was sent to, and whether or not it was accepted. Profiles now display friends based on if requests have been accepted. 

Current issue that could not be solved is that if you are adding someone who has sent you a friend request your profile does not automatically update. However leaving and returning to your/their profile will then show them as your friend.

author: rstelmokaitis
body:
On each DataReadAsync there is a byte[StreamBufferSize] allocated, in High-throughput scenarios GC pressure is quite high.
To avoid this we can use shared array pool where possible.

author: adamreeve
body:
Fixes #2 

* Updates the repo structure to use a cargo workspace so we can have a separate binary crate to generate test files
* Adds an integration test that will test reading files from a directory defined by the `PARQUET_ENCRYPTION_DATA_DIR` environment variable. This is ignored by default so it won't cause test failures when people run tests without having generated the test files.
* Also adds a Python project that can generate compatible test files and tests that will read test files
* Adds a script and GitHub action step for running integration tests. This tests all combinations of writing from either Python or Rust and reading in either Python or Rust

I'd originally thought we could use PyO3 for this but decided that would be more complex than necessary, and this approach should hopefully be simpler and easier to maintain. Plus we could potentially add tests against another implementation like parquet-java.

author: y-i
body:
This pull request introduces a new implementation of the Dinic algorithm for computing the maximum flow in a flow network. It includes the implementation of the algorithm in a header file and a usage example in a main file. The most important changes are as follows:

### Implementation of the Dinic Algorithm:

* Added a new `Dinic` class template in `MaximumFlow/dinic.hpp` to implement the Dinic maximum flow algorithm. The class supports generic numeric types and includes methods for adding edges, performing BFS and DFS, and calculating the maximum flow.
* Introduced a `Numeric` concept to enforce that the template parameter is an arithmetic type, ensuring type safety for the algorithm.

### Example Usage:

* Added a new `MaximumFlow/main.cpp` file demonstrating the usage of the `Dinic` class with an example flow network of 5 nodes. The program constructs the network, computes the maximum flow from source (node 0) to sink (node 4), and outputs the result.

Closes #2451 

## Change
<!-- Please describe the changes you made. -->
Due to some chroma bugs, I changed the support version of chroma from 0.6.3 to 1.0.0 (which was released right after 0.6.3, please refer to https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/releases)
Update the support of V2 API, now supports different operations using Chroma V2 API
Several changes should be paid attention to in the V2 API
1. For the embedding add operation, we need to keep a consistent number of IDs, embeddings, documents, URIs, and metadatas, so we can not just leave documents and metadatas null
2. V2 API implemented the metadata filters
3. V2 delete collection API, it's delete by id in the docs, but in practice, it's delete by name

Fix the tests that are not compatible with V2 API

Updated to version 3.0.0b, which is a complete Nextflow/Singularity & Bioconda/Docker refactoring. ---- Please read the [guidelines for Bioconda recipes](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/guidelines.html) before opening a pull request (PR). ### General instructions * If this PR adds or updates a recipe, use "Add" or "Update" appropriately as the first word in its title. * New recipes not directly relevant to the biological sciences need to be submitted to the [conda-forge channel](https://conda-forge.org/docs/) instead of Bioconda. * PRs require reviews prior to being merged. Once your PR is passing tests and ready to be merged, please issue the `@BiocondaBot please add label` command. * Please post questions [on Gitter](https://gitter.im/bioconda/Lobby) or ping `@bioconda/core` in a comment. ### Instructions for avoiding API, ABI, and CLI breakage issues Conda is able to record and lock (a.k.a. pin) dependency versions used at build time of other recipes. This way, one can avoid that expectations of a downstream recipe with regards to API, ABI, or CLI are violated by later changes in the recipe. If not already present in the meta.yaml, make sure to specify `run_exports` (see [here](https://bioconda.github.io/contributor/linting.html#missing-run-exports) for the rationale and comprehensive explanation). Add a `run_exports` section like this: ```yaml build: run_exports: - ... ``` with `...` being one of: | Case | run_exports statement | | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | semantic versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x") }}` | | semantic versioning (0.x.x) | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` | | known breakage in minor versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | known breakage in patch versions | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin="x.x.x") }}` (in such a case, please add a note that shortly mentions your evidence for that) | | calendar versioning | `{{ pin_subpackage("myrecipe", max_pin=None) }}` | while replacing `"myrecipe"` with either `name` if a `name|lower` variable is defined in your recipe or with the lowercase name of the package in quotes. ### Bot commands for PR management
Please use the following BiocondaBot commands: Everyone has access to the following BiocondaBot commands, which can be given in a comment:
@BiocondaBot please update Merge the master branch into a PR.
@BiocondaBot please add label Add the please review & merge label.
@BiocondaBot please fetch artifacts Post links to CI-built packages/containers.
You can use this to test packages locally.
Note that the @BiocondaBot please merge command is now depreciated. Please just squash and merge instead. Also, the bot watches for comments from non-members that include `@bioconda/` and will automatically re-post them to notify the addressed ``.

body:
This pull request introduces several updates, including new dependencies, UI components, and routing adjustments. The most significant changes involve the addition of reusable UI components, updates to the sidebar functionality, and modifications to the routing structure.

### UI Components and Utilities:
* Added new reusable components: `BadgeStatusColor` for status display (`src/components/BadgeStatusColor.tsx`), `Collapsible` for collapsible sections (`src/components/ui/collapsible.tsx`), `Sheet` for modal-like UI (`src/components/ui/sheet.tsx`), `Skeleton` for loading placeholders (`src/components/ui/skeleton.tsx`), and `Tooltip` for tooltips (`src/components/ui/tooltip.tsx`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b21e34837825df26f2235de90f213a142746bb6b0922caeec9011e4c7de9d69cR1-R19) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-461fb61d557f4461b6f25584b5aa3902b01376d9f0eb4db43d94630a3c41ed2dR1-R33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-319e19004d72883ad55ee0b5035771b79f614157b68d255d86a036a1dc78876eR1-R142) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8b049a29fbe399422d407b74c69619d6ad1bb9da0df052ec11f0bf664dcad4f2R1-R16) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a79400767c2d21e11b1356a6bc9bf6b2e9d4c75968139f99e7e3f11276525f68R1-R50)

* Added a `useIsMobile` hook to detect mobile screen sizes dynamically.

### Sidebar Enhancements:
* Introduced the `AppSidebar` component, which dynamically renders navigation items based on user roles (`warehouse`, `driver`, or `outlet`). This includes dropdown menus for team selection and user information.

* Integrated the sidebar into the `AuthLayout`, replacing the placeholder `Navbar` and adding a `SidebarProvider` for managing sidebar state. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-59bda12c4e8e65e86bbc5199d50950a3929a8f8771c7e08ec2ba1cf6c3b01c64R4-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-59bda12c4e8e65e86bbc5199d50950a3929a8f8771c7e08ec2ba1cf6c3b01c64L18-R33)

### Routing Updates:
* Moved the `/request-order` route from the warehouse section to the outlet section in `App.tsx`. This aligns with the role-based navigation structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-26ad4b834941d9b19ebf9db8082bd202aaf72ea0ddea85f5a8a0cb3c729cc6f2L38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-26ad4b834941d9b19ebf9db8082bd202aaf72ea0ddea85f5a8a0cb3c729cc6f2R51)

### Dependency Updates:
* Added `@radix-ui/react-collapsible` and `@radix-ui/react-tooltip` to support the new UI components.

### Table Enhancements:
* Updated `TableHistoryOrder` to use the new `BadgeStatusColor` component for displaying order statuses with color-coded badges. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1b082ef58c607e8e05af3fd066dfdea90172ae6c4f4ee9fbd592935d271c541bL12-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1b082ef58c607e8e05af3fd066dfdea90172ae6c4f4ee9fbd592935d271c541bL46-R50)

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [dev.zacsweers.metro](https://redirect.github.com/ZacSweers/metro) | plugin | minor | `0.2.0` -> `0.3.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>ZacSweers/metro (dev.zacsweers.metro)</summary>

### [`v0.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/ZacSweers/metro/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#030)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/ZacSweers/metro/compare/0.2.0...0.3.0)

*2025-05-05*

-   **New**: Add support for `@ContributesGraphExtension`! See the [docs](https://zacsweers.github.io/metro/dependency-graphs#contributed-graph-extensions) for more info.
-   **New**: Add a `asContribution()` compiler intrinsic to upcast graphs to expected contribution types. For example: `val contributedInterface = appGraph.asContribution<ContributedInterface>()`. This is validated at compile-time.
-   **New**: Automatically transform `@Provides` functions to be `private`. This is enabled by defaults and supersedes the `publicProviderSeverity` when enabled, and can be disabled via the Gradle extension or `transform-providers-to-private` compiler option. Note that properties and providers with any annotations with `KClass` arguments are not supported yet pending upstream kotlinc changes.
-   **Enhancement**: Rewrite the internal `BindingGraph` implementation to be more performant, accurate, and testable.
-   **Enhancement**: Add diagnostic to check that graph factories don't provide their target graphs as parameters.
-   **Enhancement**: Add diagnostic to check that a primary scope is defined if any additionalScopes are also defined on a graph annotation.
-   **Enhancement**: Add diagnostic to validate that contributed types do not have narrower visibility that aggregating graphs. i.e. detect if you accidentally try to contribute an `internal` type to a `public` graph.
-   **Enhancement**: Optimize supertype lookups when building binding classes by avoiding previously visited classes.
-   **Enhancement**: Don't generate hints for contributed types with non-public API visibility.
-   **Enhancement**: When reporting duplicate binding errors where one of the bindings is contributed, report the contributing class in the error message.
-   **Enhancement**: When reporting scope incompatibility, check any extended parents match the scope and suggest a workaround in the error diagnostic.
-   **Enhancement**: Allow AssistedFactory methods to be protected.
-   **Fix**: Fix incremental compilation when a parent graph or supertype modifies/removes a provider.
-   **Fix**: Fix rank processing error when the outranked binding is contributed using Metro's ContributesBinding annotation.
-   **Fix**: Fix `@Provides` graph parameters not getting passed on to extended child graphs.
-   **Fix**: Fix qualifiers on bindings not getting seen by extended child graphs.
-   **Fix**: Fix qualifiers getting ignored on accessors from `@Includes` dependencies.
-   **Fix**: Fix transitive scoped dependencies not always getting initialized first in graph provider fields.
-   **Fix**: Fix injected `lateinit var` properties being treated as if they have default values.
-   **Fix**: Alias bindings not always having their backing type visited during graph validation.
-   **Fix**: Fix race condition in generating parent graphs first even if child graph is encountered first in processing.
-   **Fix**: Fallback `AssistedInjectChecker` error report to the declaration source.
-   **Fix**: Fix missing parent supertype bindings in graph extensions.
-   **Change**: `InstanceFactory` is no longer a value class. This wasn't going to offer much value in practice.
-   **Change**: Change debug reports dir to be per-compilation rather than per-platform.

Special thanks to [@​gabrielittner](https://redirect.github.com/gabrielittner), [@​kevinguitar](https://redirect.github.com/kevinguitar), [@​JoelWilcox](https://redirect.github.com/JoelWilcox), and [@​japplin](https://redirect.github.com/japplin) for contributing to this release!

# Overview

The issue is that the default map layer of PygeoAPI is set to Canada (Montreal). Users will see this map when there is not valid coordinate data for PygeoAPI to use. The default map has been adjusted to the map of Australia. 

# Related issue / discussion

https://gajira.atlassian.net/browse/DAT-1003

# Additional information

# Dependency policy (RFC2)

- [ ] I have ensured that this PR meets [RFC2](https://pygeoapi.io/development/rfc/2) requirements

# Updates to public demo

  - [ ] https://github.com/geopython/demo.pygeoapi.io/blob/master/services/pygeoapi_master/local.config.yml

This PR moves to allow the last.fm rich presence plugin to load secrets from a path. Used in combination with a credential manager it can provide a more secure way to store credentials.

## Summary
- Fixed manifest.json missing from extension build
- Fixed HTML structure in options.html and sidepanel.html to properly fill the screen
- Fixed button state toggling to prevent multiple states showing at once
- Added standalone logout.js script for improved authentication flow
- Enhanced dark mode support with complete theme system
- Improved the build process to include all necessary files
- Created new extension.zip with proper file structure
- Converted all JavaScript files to TypeScript for better type safety

## Detailed Changes
- Updated options.html and sidepanel.html with proper viewport-filling layout
- Improved the setLoadingState function to properly toggle visible states

author: fahmi-ramadhan
body:
This PR fixes two related issues where incomplete data was being sent to Meilisearch, causing data loss in search results:

1. When publishing an itinerary (issue #122), only partial data was sent to Meilisearch
2. When updating the like count of an itinerary (issue #123), only like count and basic user info were included

## Changes
- Updated `publishItinerary` method to fetch complete itinerary data (with all sections, blocks, tags) before sending to Meilisearch
- Fixed `_updateLikeCount` method to include all related entities when retrieving itinerary data
- Added a conditional check in `_updateLikeCount` to only update published itineraries in the search index
- Enhanced the `addOrUpdateItinerary` method to be more explicit about only indexing published itineraries

## Testing
- Created an itinerary with multiple sections and blocks
- Published the itinerary and verified all data appears in search results
- Liked the itinerary with another account and confirmed all data remains intact in search results
- Unpublished the itinerary and verified it was removed from search index

## Fixes
Closes #122
Closes #123

author: yuhsuan-hwang
body:
**Description**

This PR is for #2492: channel map coordinate overlay related enhancements. The overlay in channel map mode are adjusted so that they are consistent with the overlays in non-channel map mode.

Code changes

* Created a new store `OverlaySettings` for the shared settings in the image view settings widget. `OverlayStore` becomes frame-dependent.
* Unified variable naming in `OverlayStore` and `ChannelMapViewComponent`, with detailed documentation added in `OverlayStore`.
* Created `OverlayStore` for PV previews and channel map outer and inner part.
* Adjusted the redraw algorithm in `ChannelMapInnerOverlayComponent`: a canvas is created for each channel, and the refs to all canvases are stored in a map ([ref](https://18.react.dev/learn/manipulating-the-dom-with-refs#how-to-manage-a-list-of-refs-using-a-ref-callback)). A draw function is called in `OverlayComponent` to redraw all canvases.
* Moved the image view widget width/height from `OverlayStore` to `AppStore`.
* Moved the PV preview widget width/height from `FrameStore` to `PvGeneratorWidgetStore`.
* Moved frame-dependent colorbar variables `yOffset`, `height`, `tickNum` from `OverlayStore` to `ColorbarStore`.
* Removed optional props in `ColorbarComponent`, `OverlayComponent`, and `ToolbarComponent`.
* Removed unused prop `overlaySettings` in `RegionViewComponent`.
* Changed `OverlaySettings.base` and `OverlaySettings.defaultGap` from computed getter functions to regular fields.

Tested that (with devicePixelRatio = 1 and 2)

* The wcs overlay does not appear blurry in channel map mode.
* The wcs overlay remains correct when the number of visible channels is less than row × column.
* Labels, title, cursor info, and (right/top/bottom) colorbar remain unchanged when switching between channel map and non-channel map modes.
* The outermost borders (top, bottom, left, right) remain unchanged with different row num and column num in channel map mode (there may be a 1-pixel difference in gaps).
* There is no gap between the raster canvas and the wcs overlay border in channel map mode.
* The active channel highlight border is roughly symmetric to the wcs overlay border (there may be a 1-pixel difference with difference row num and column num). There is no gap between the active channel highlight border and the wcs overlay border.
* The regions and channel labels are placed correctly in channel map mode.
* The wcs overlay remains correct in single/multi-panel mode and PV previews.

~ToDo: update to latest dev after #2512 is merged.~

We use the `DamagedHelmet` glTF asset in many demos. To add a bit more variety, I have updated the the tone mapping demos for WebGL and WebGPU renderer with a new one. Since the scene already uses an environment map that shows Venice, I though something cultural from that place would be nice. I've found a very aesthetic mask asset at Sketchfab that makes the demos more visual appealing. Thanks to `gltf-transform`, I was able to compress it under 5 MB without loosing much of its fidelity. The original size was over 40 MB.

author: mshojaei-txfusion
body:
### Description

Add Warp Route Config interface standardization across all registry implementations by introducing a consistent `addWarpRouteConfig` method to the `IRegistry` interface and refactoring implementations to use a unified approach.

### Backward compatibility

No - Removes the overloaded string parameter version of `addWarpRouteConfig` in FileSystemRegistry which was previously maintained for backward compatibility.

### Related issues
https://github.com/hyperlane-xyz/hyperlane-monorepo/issues/5244

### Testing

The standardized API has been tested with internal Hyperlane registry operations. All registry implementation classes have been updated to properly implement the new interface method.

### What does this PR do?

Exclude DDCI environment variables from the list that's used to compute the cache key

These variables include the PR number, among other things, which almost guarantees a systematic cache miss, except for consecutive builds of the same PR.

author: rita-codes
body:
This PR fixes the following **issue**: [https://github.com/mui/mui-x/issues/15649](https://github.com/mui/mui-x/issues/15649)

### Cause
The issue was in the `useTreeViewKeyboardNavigation` hook, as @flaviendelangle pointed out, specifically in the following line inside the loop:
```
lastNavigableChild = selectorItemOrderedChildrenIds(state, currentItemId).find((childId) =>
  selectorCanItemBeFocused(state, childId),
);
```
This uses `.find(...)`, which returns the first focusable child, not the last one.
As a result, when navigating down into the previous sibling’s descendants, we incorrectly select the **first** child ("1 2 1") instead of the **last** visible focusable item ("1 2 5").

### Fix

- `getLastNavigableItemInArray` correctly returns the last focusable item in the subtree, so we don’t need to override it with `.find(...)`. By simply removing the `.find(...)` step and reusing `getLastNavigableItemInArray` in the loop, we ensure that the navigation behaves as expected, it goes to the last focusable descendant of the previous sibling.

- Added two tests to cover this case and prevent regressions

### Demo
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0306c4d3-7289-4b6e-9cb4-022598f69554

author: roosterfish
body:
Preceded by:
* https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/15775
* https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/15776
* https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/15777
* https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/15859

### Overview

This PR uses the new backup config metadata format introduced in https://github.com/canonical/lxd/pull/15129 to track all of an instance's custom storage volumes.
In addition all of the storage volume's storage pools are now listed too.

Whenever a custom volume (or its snapshots) gets updated, LXD has to check whether or not this custom volume is attached to any instance. If it's attached, with the changes proposed in this PR, LXD rewrites the backup config file to propagate the latest state of the volume.

### Detail

In order to pick up an instance's custom volume changes, the outcome of such a change has to be persisted in the parent instance's backup config.
LXD currently only has support for `GenerateCustomVolumeBackupConfig` which produces a backup config file (using the standard format) to be included in custom volume exports.

This PR grows a new `UpdateCustomVolumeBackupFile` (same as `UpdateInstanceBackupFile`) which allows updates of a custom volume to be persisted to file. With the only difference that those updates are written to all the instances using the custom volume.

As multiple instances can use the same volume, looking up all the necessary information to rebuild an instance's backup config might be resource intensive. Therefore the instance grows another `GenerateInstanceCustomVolumeBackupConfig` function which allows generating the backup config for the instance's custom volumes by leveraging caching mechanisms. Also an already prepared backup config can now be passed down to `GenerateInstanceBackupConfig` and `UpdateInstanceBackupFile` if its already crafted from the cache.

Having the `GenerateInstanceCustomVolumeBackupConfig` exported on the `Pool` interface allows arbitrary callers to either generate the custom volume's config to be passed when creating an instance's backup config or simply provide nothing. This is helpful in the case of exporting instances as the received backup doesn't contain any information about custom volumes attached to the respective instance.

Fixes https://github.com/canonical/lxd/issues/11712

# 🛡️ Feature: Authentication & Task Enhancements

## 요약
이번 PR에서는 다음의 주요 기능을 추가·개선합니다:

1. **비밀번호 보안 강화**  
   - bcrypt 기반 해싱 유틸리티 추가  
   - 유저 생성 시 해싱된 비밀번호 저장  
2. **JWT 로그인 / 보호된 엔드포인트**  
   - JWT 토큰 발급 유틸리티 추가  
   - `/token` 로그인 엔드포인트 구현  
   - `Authorization: Bearer <token>` 헤더를 통해 보호된 라우터 접근 제어  
3. **Docker 환경 세팅**  
   - JWT 의존성(python-jose, bcrypt 등) 및 시스템 라이브러리 설치  
   - `Dockerfile` 업데이트 및 `docker-compose` 볼륨/캐시 설정 개선  
4. **Task API 확장**  
   - Task 모델에 확장된 필드(user_id 포함) 적용  
   - 생성·조회·수정·삭제 API 추가 및 curl 테스트 완료  

---

## 📋 커밋 히스토리
- `feat(auth): 비밀번호 해싱 유틸 추가 및 유저 생성 시 적용`  
- `feat(auth): JWT 토큰 발급 유틸리티 추가`  
- `feat(auth): JWT 로그인 토큰 발급 API 구현`  
- `feat(jwt): JWT 사용 도커 세팅`  
- `test: jwt 적용 및 token curl 테스트`  
- `test: 보호된 엔드포인트 테스트`  
- `test: JWT 인증 curl 테스트 완료`  
- `feat(task): 확장된 필드를 포함한 태스크 작업 및 curl 테스트 완료`  

---

## ✅ 주요 변경 사항

### 1️⃣ Authentication
- `app/utils/security.py`  
  - `get_password_hash()`, `verify_password()` 함수 도입  
  - `create_access_token()`, `decode_access_token()` 생성  
- `app/routers/auth.py`  
  - `/token` (로그인) 엔드포인트  
- `app/routers/user.py`  
  - 유저 생성 시 해시된 비밀번호 저장  
  - 보호된 라우트 예시(`/users/me`) 구현  

### 2️⃣ Protected Endpoints
- `Depends(get_current_user)` 적용으로 인증된 사용자만 접근 가능  
- `401 Unauthorized` 처리 및 에러 메시지 일관화  

### 3️⃣ Docker & CI 환경
- `Dockerfile`에 `libpq-dev`, `libffi-dev`, `gcc` 설치  
- `pdm install` 캐시 무시 설정 및 `.venv` 초기화  
- `docker-compose.yml` 볼륨 마운트 및 rebuild 자동화 섹션 정리  

### 4️⃣ Task API 확장
- `schemas/task.py` → `user_id` 필드 포함  
- `crud/task.py`, `routers/task.py`  
  - Task 생성·조회·수정·삭제 기능 완전 구현  
- Curl 스크립트로 전 기능 검증 완료  

---

## 🔧 테스트 체크리스트

```bash
# 1. 유저 생성 & 해시 확인
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/users/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice","password":"secret","is_teacher":false}'

# 2. 로그인 (JWT 발급)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "username=alice&password=secret"

# 3. 보호된 엔드포인트 접근
TOKEN=<발급된_JWT>
curl -X GET http://localhost:8000/users/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# 4. Task CRUD
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/tasks/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Test Task","status":"TODO","user_id":1}'
curl -X GET http://localhost:8000/tasks/?skip=0&limit=10 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8000/tasks/1 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Updated","status":"DONE"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/tasks/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

author: mihe
body:
#91006 introduced a minor regression with how errors are printed for the case where there are no script backtraces, where they now add empty lines after the `at:` part, one for every registered script language:

```
ERROR: Expected Image data size of 256x256x1 (DXT5 RGBA8 with 8 mipmaps) = 87408 bytes, got 87360 bytes instead.
   at: initialize_data (./core/io/image.cpp:2230)

ERROR: Invalid image: image is empty
   at: create_from_image (./scene/resources/image_texture.cpp:77)

ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://broken.dds. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
   at: _load (./core/io/resource_loader.cpp:342)
```

This PR fixes that by checking whether the backtraces are empty before printing them, in all the relevant places.

Note that this could also be fixed in a less intrusive way, by simply changing `Engine.capture_script_backtraces` to not include empty backtraces at all, but I'm personally of the opinion that a backtrace should always be returned for every registered script language, to clearly indicate that there are indeed no stack frames for that particular script language.

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes to the map and room selection functionality in the app. Key changes include improving the pulse animation for better visual feedback, refactoring `MapWidget` to a stateful widget for dynamic updates, and adding utility methods for polygon calculations. These updates enhance user experience and code maintainability.

### Enhancements to map and room visualization:
* Improved the pulse animation by reducing its duration and adjusting its scale for smoother visual feedback.
* Enhanced the map to visually highlight "from" and "to" rooms with distinct pulsing animations and added room name labels that dynamically adjust based on zoom level. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7b0460bd3a8cd4898f0e228e676c9910324ed9be12b8eab0e08425e9e6fa0233R38-R84) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7b0460bd3a8cd4898f0e228e676c9910324ed9be12b8eab0e08425e9e6fa0233L56-R307)

### Refactoring for flexibility and maintainability:
* Refactored `MapWidget` from a stateless to a stateful widget, enabling dynamic updates such as zoom level and map rotation tracking. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7b0460bd3a8cd4898f0e228e676c9910324ed9be12b8eab0e08425e9e6fa0233L2-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7b0460bd3a8cd4898f0e228e676c9910324ed9be12b8eab0e08425e9e6fa0233R38-R84)
* Added new properties `fromRoom` and `toRoom` to `MapWidget` for highlighting specific rooms on the map.

### Utility methods for polygon calculations:
* Introduced `calculatePolygonCenter`, `isPointInPolygon`, and related helper methods in a new `polygon_utils.dart` file to calculate room label positions and ensure they are inside polygons.

### Bug fixes:
* Fixed a potential null-pointer issue when comparing selected polygons by using null-aware operators.

These changes collectively improve the app's usability and maintainability while laying the groundwork for more advanced map interactions.- changed the homescreen to accomodate the animation of the selected rooms
- changed map widget to be stateful, to keep track of the to and from rooms.
- changed map widget to allow for the animation of the polygons when selected for canclulations
- changed map widget to show names on the rooms
- added polygon utils to calculate polygon centers, isPointInPolygon, finding visual center, and distance calculations

author: dylancochran
body:
I was gonna wait to open the PR, but based on what I tested real quick, it seems as if nothing broke so I have no need to hold off.

Some stuff has been changed, fellas. First of all, let me direct your attention to the events model,

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0171a3a3-33ae-476d-9e9a-7c876d1dd52b)

ru_name and ru_description has been added for multilingual support. "Thumbnail_url" has been dropped because you can always infer strapi thumbnail url from standard image url (p much just slap a thumbnail_ leading I believe), "published" boolean has been added, "roles" for who is allowed to edit the event, and "mock" has been deleted since we no longer actually need it.

Permissions Management, Event Editor, and Event Manager permissions have been fully fleshed out (See the Readme for a full list of permissions under work)

Let's speak of changes, first and foremost mild fixing for alignment in all table types has been done, the tables will look a bit better.

Also, user id is now visible in the users table, because I figure why not it may be useful down the road (consider if we implement some sort of automated role fixing based off uid or something else, it costs nothing to add it so I have chosen to do so)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a3069b0-9dcb-492f-b4d8-5e21d63516d8)
Here is an example of creating a permission, some changes include
- Admin is NO LONGER able to be assigned, it makes the most sense to restrict that to the default Administrator role the more I think about it
- Proper restrictions are put in place for what roles can be added to roles based on your permissions (see readme for more details)

Edit Role, and Delete Role have ALSO been properly accounted for, permissions-wise.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b486c0c-56d6-42c2-8d90-aa973133812a)
When assigning a user roles, it PROPERLY checks that the assigner has the proper permissions now based on the rules described in the readme.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5242c9d2-684c-4597-aaba-1c5cdc732a78)
In the create event dialog, there are new options, the ability to pick event locks. You can only choose ones that you have access to according to rules defined in the readme. Create, edit, and delete event all completely have permissions implemented, roles-based access for events has been implemented.

In summary, permissions is COMPLETELY implemented for Role Management, User Management, and Events.

author: yasasr1
body:
## Purpose
The existing Organization Resource Resolver service provides two main capabilities:

- Retrieving resources by traversing the hierarchy of a given organization and application.
- Retrieving resources by traversing the hierarchy of a given organization.

This PR extracts the application-specific traversal logic into a separate service.
The goal is to prevent cyclic dependencies that can occur when the Organization Resource Resolver is invoked within the idp-mgt service (or any other service that app-mgt service depends on)

Since this PR introduces significant refactoring to the Organization Resource Resolver service, a major version bump will be performed to reflect the breaking changes.

## Description

The various `Provides-Extra` sections in the built wheel's `METADATA` file were shuffled arbitrarily between different builds, which made it more difficult to detect other reproducibility issues (see https://reproducible-builds.org/).  There doesn't seem any reason for `EXTENSIONS` here to be a set; a tuple will work just as well, and adds an ordering guarantee.

This PR contains a very basic implementation for performance - measuring duration of execution of sync command.
There is code duplication, and it's been implemented to run on only latest enterprise gateway - so needs polishing.

IMO, depending on duration could lead to flaky tests - as network latency is unpredictable.

Ideally, I'd want to have the following in a performance test:
1. No flakiness
2. Key performance indicators - CPU consumption, memory consumption, Network throughput, and execution time, for example
3. Representative state files to measure each - designed to stress each of the key performance indicators
4. Storing past metrics and easy comparison - for example, i'd want the execution time on `main` available to compare with my `feat/slow-feature` as a comment on my PR - so it's easy to compare what is changing.

Feedback and thoughts on how this can be improved welcome 🙏

body:
<!-- Please create (if there is not one yet) a issue before sending a PR -->
<!-- Add issue number (Eg: fixes #123) -->
<!-- Always provide changes in existing tests or new tests -->

Fixes #6

### Checklist
- [x] My branch is up-to-date with upstream/develop branch.
- [x] Everything works and tested for Python 3.8.0 and above.
- [x] I ran pre-commit checks against my changes.
- [x] I've written tests against my changes and all the current present tests are passing.

### Current behaviour
The previous health check mechanism for Dramatiq-based workers (`SnapshotAsyncWorker`, `AggregationAsyncWorker`, `ProcessorDistributor`) relied on checking the liveness of a manually managed `threading.Thread` object (`_worker_thread`). This approach was flawed because:
1. The lifecycle of the manual thread didn't accurately reflect the state of Dramatiq's internal worker threads.
2. It could lead to false negatives (reporting the thread as dead when Dramatiq workers were still processing) or false positives (failing to detect hung or crashed Dramatiq workers).
3. The `IPFSUnpinningWorker` health check also needed refinement to correctly monitor its primary task.

### New expected behaviour
This PR implements a robust, active health check mechanism specifically for Dramatiq workers and refines the check for the IPFS worker:
1.  **Dramatiq Workers (`SnapshotAsyncWorker`, `AggregationAsyncWorker`, `ProcessorDistributor`):**
    *   Removes the manual `_worker_thread` management.
    *   Introduces dedicated health check queues (`HEALTH_QUEUE_NAME`) and actors (`health_ping_snapshot`, `health_ping_agg`, `health_ping_dist`).
    *   The main process's `_periodic_health_reporter` task now periodically sends a ping message (containing the worker's hostname) to the respective health queue.
    *   The health ping actor consumes this message and updates a hash field for the specific hostname within the shared `service_health_timestamps_key` in Redis.
    *   The `_periodic_health_reporter` verifies that the timestamp for its hostname in `service_health_timestamps_key` is recent (within `interval + 30s`). Failure to update indicates unresponsive Dramatiq workers.

This ensures that health checks accurately reflect whether the core processing units (Dramatiq workers or the main IPFS task) are responsive.

### Change logs

#### Changed
- Refactored health check mechanism for Dramatiq-based workers (`SnapshotAsyncWorker`, `AggregationAsyncWorker`, `ProcessorDistributor`) to use an active ping/ack pattern via dedicated Dramatiq queues and actors.
- Modified `_periodic_health_reporter` in Dramatiq workers to send health pings and check timestamps in Redis (`service_health_timestamps_key`) instead of checking thread liveness.
- Adjusted logging levels in health reporters across workers to reduce noise during normal operation (logs success at DEBUG, failures at WARNING/CRITICAL).
- Updated Dramatiq `Worker` instantiations to listen on both main task queues and the new health check queues.
- Refactored `run` methods in Dramatiq workers to directly manage the `dramatiq.Worker` lifecycle (`start`/`stop`) instead of using manual threads.

#### Removed
- Manual `_worker_thread` attribute and associated management logic in `SnapshotAsyncWorker`, `AggregationAsyncWorker`, and `ProcessorDistributor`.
- Unused `dramatiq_worker_health_key` Redis key function.
- Unused `threading` and `Optional` imports where applicable.

## Deployment Instructions
Standard deployment process.

author: jurooravec
body:
This PR modifies our monkeypatching of Django's `Template.render()` to call `render_dependencies()` from within there, as [mentioned here](https://github.com/django-components/django-components/issues/968#issuecomment-2653965260).

This practically means we no longer need the middleware, so I removed it too.

This also adds a `"raw"` strategy (I called this strategy `"none"` before, but `"raw"` fits better IMO). This is to be used when you want to tell components NOT to process the JS / CSS. This replaces the `render_dependencies=False` which previously could have been passed to `Component.render()`.

```py
Table.render(
    kwargs={...},
    deps_strategy="raw",
)
```

Also, to be able to set the strategy when rendering templates with `Template.render()` or `django.shortcuts.render()`, users can set `DJC_DEPS_STRATEGY` context variable:

```py
from django.shortcuts import render

render(request, "my_template.html", {"DJC_DEPS_STRATEGY": "fragment"})
```

Closes https://github.com/django-components/django-components/issues/968, closes https://github.com/django-components/django-components/pull/972

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive overhaul of the LearnWith authentication backend, migrating the database from PostgreSQL/Prisma to MongoDB/Mongoose, setting up Docker-based workflows, and implementing development tooling for code quality and consistency. The changes span configuration files, environment setup, Docker support, and application code updates, ensuring a modernized and streamlined backend.

### Database Migration and Application Updates:
* Migrated from PostgreSQL/Prisma to MongoDB/Mongoose, updating dependencies, file structure, and authentication logic. Key changes include adding Mongoose models (`src/modules/user/user.model.ts`) and a MongoDB connection plugin (`src/plugins/mongoose.ts`) while removing Prisma-related files. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c1603ee6a674bb75255aa448057630506153e363297fd58668e6679f10909bc6R1-R85)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-841254fe75488c1bd4cd7f68f00b4be0e48dcfbc4a16b45847b68295e0e3b27bR1-R104)`)
* Updated `src/app.ts` to register plugins for MongoDB, JWT, and OAuth2, and added error handling for better debugging and stability. (`[src/app.tsR1-R104](diffhunk://#diff-841254fe75488c1bd4cd7f68f00b4be0e48dcfbc4a16b45847b68295e0e3b27bR1-R104)`)

### Docker and Deployment Enhancements:
* Added a multi-stage `Dockerfile` for optimized builds and a `docker-compose.yml` file to run the application with MongoDB in a containerized environment. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dd2c0eb6ea5cfc6c4bd4eac30934e2d5746747af48fef6da689e85b752f39557R1-R50)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3R1-R46)`)
* Introduced a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`) for building and publishing Docker images. (`[.github/workflows/docker-publish.ymlR1-R57](diffhunk://#diff-5b21991be47c2922383bdc0b6bf00b65af7db51b82d049dd8d6ad03e3d37ac98R1-R57)`)

### Development Tooling and Configuration:
* Configured ESLint and Prettier for consistent code formatting and linting, with rules tailored for TypeScript. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a32a0887ed9d1d707bbb3b845b7df7fd40e673c47e7b60a3ebd896b68d3b8839R1-R44)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-663ade211b3a1552162de21c4031fcd16be99407aae5ceecbb491a2efc43d5d2R1-R7)`)
* Integrated Husky and lint-staged for pre-commit and pre-push hooks to enforce code quality. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d2bc4bbf14eadc292d84e0ef5f7a93115c23557f533809fc80b896934291529dR1-R4)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43bbc75a027a43baaddc57670d8ab49b4aa2981053c3cabba17567723d3a9fb6R1-R4)`)

### Documentation Improvements:
* Updated `README.md` with detailed setup instructions, API endpoints, and authentication flow. Added `MIGRATION.md` to document the database migration process. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R109)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1603ee6a674bb75255aa448057630506153e363297fd58668e6679f10909bc6R1-R85)`)
* Added `docker-readme.md` to guide developers on using Docker for local development and production. (`[docker-readme.mdR1-R138](diffhunk://#diff-bc457b153b4e9f6d89d0a23e4293dd715bdfb0ae7bd7d22b252d18a38623e616R1-R138)`)

### Environment and Build Configurations:

# Implement Mobile App Functionality with RevenueCat Integration

This PR implements mobile app functionality for the budget and collection management app, focusing on:

- Converting the existing web app to mobile platforms (Android and iOS)
- Implementing premium subscription features with RevenueCat integration
- Fixing TypeScript translation string errors
- Configuring Capacitor for mobile deployment

## Changes

### RevenueCat Integration
- Created RevenueCat configuration file with platform-specific settings
- Updated SubscriptionContext to handle mobile in-app purchases
- Added methods for purchasing, restoring, and managing subscriptions
- Implemented platform detection to use different subscription flows on web vs mobile

### Capacitor Configuration
- Updated capacitor.config.ts with proper settings for mobile deployment
- Added keyboard and splash screen configurations
- Set up proper build output directory for Next.js static export

### UI/UX Improvements
- Fixed translation issues in BottomNavigation and PageHeader components
- Added mobile-specific subscription handling in plans page
- Implemented real-time price fetching from app stores

### Build System
- Added mobile-specific build scripts to package.json
- Set up proper export configuration for Next.js static site generation
- Fixed Android build compatibility issues with Java 17
- Resolved SDK version conflicts in Android configuration
- Added patch for Android 15 compatibility issues in CapacitorWebView.java

## Android Setup Instructions

To build the Android app locally, you need to:

1. Create a `local.properties` file in the `android` directory with your Android SDK location:
   ```
   sdk.dir=C:\\Users\\USERNAME\\AppData\\Local\\Android\\Sdk
   ```
   Replace `USERNAME` with your Windows username.

2. See detailed instructions in [docs/android-setup.md](docs/android-setup.md)

## Build Instructions

1. Install dependencies:
   ```
   npm install
   ```
   This will automatically apply the necessary patches to fix Android 15 compatibility issues.

2. Build the Next.js app (generates the 'out' directory):
   ```
   npm run build
   ```

3. Sync with Capacitor (copies web assets to Android/iOS):
   ```
   npm run cap:sync
   ```

4. Build the Android app:
   ```
   cd android
   ./gradlew build
   ```

## Android 15 Compatibility Fix

This PR includes a patch for Android 15 compatibility issues in CapacitorWebView.java. The patch is automatically applied during the `npm install` process via the postinstall script. This fixes compilation errors related to:

- `Build.VERSION_CODES.VANILLA_ICE_CREAM` - Android 15 specific constant
- `android.R.attr.windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement` - Android 15 specific attribute

## Testing
- Tested TypeScript compilation with `npm run typecheck`
- Verified RevenueCat integration with mock data
- Tested UI rendering on mobile screen sizes
- Successfully built Android app with Gradle

## Summary

Fixes #4903

## Changes proposed

* updates feature flag logic to allow hardcoded values to be properly used if env var values are missing 
* updates default feature flag values for flags recently turned on in production to true

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->

A bug existed in the frontend feature flag default logic that would effectively not honor the hardcoded defaults set in the application. This will not be an issue in deployed environments, where environment variable based values are set for all feature flags that will override the defaults, but for local development this made it difficult to rely on desired default behavior without remembering to set command line env vars each time you start a server.

Fixing this involves moving the `string -> boolean` logic for the env vars to later in the process

Note that to get this working I had to:

* work around the fact that lodash cannot be imported into any file used in Next's middleware
* tracked down a tbd error around a reference to the document in server side pre-rendered code...

3. start a local server on main with `npm run dev`

5. _VERIFY_: login button does not appear in header

Potential fix for [https://github.com/johansenmwesigwa/volunteering-app/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/johansenmwesigwa/volunteering-app/security/code-scanning/1)

To address the issue, we will add rate limiting to the routes in `backend/routes/opportunityRoutes.js`. The `express-rate-limit` package will be used to implement this. A rate limiter will be configured to allow a maximum of 100 requests per 15 minutes for the `/` route. This will mitigate the risk of DoS attacks by limiting the number of requests a client can make within a specified time window.

Steps to fix:
1. Install the `express-rate-limit` package if it is not already installed.
2. Import the `express-rate-limit` package in the file.
3. Configure a rate limiter with appropriate settings (e.g., 100 requests per 15 minutes).
4. Apply the rate limiter to the route handler for `GET /`.

## Purpose
This pull request makes significant updates to the `knowledge_mining_api.ipynb` notebook and its dependencies, focusing on transitioning to asynchronous programming, improving functionality, and updating the environment configuration. Below is a summary of the most important changes:

### Transition to Asynchronous Programming
* Converted synchronous methods (`get_db_connection`, `execute_sql_query`, `greeting`, `get_SQL_Response`, and `get_answers_from_calltranscripts`) to asynchronous equivalents, enabling better scalability and performance for I/O-bound operations. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL37-R45)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL65-R87)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL124-R117)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL171-R161)`, `[[5]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL220-R308)`)

### Enhancements to SQL Query Execution
* Improved the `execute_sql_query` function to handle database connections and cursors more robustly using `try-finally` blocks, ensuring proper cleanup of resources. (`[microhack_workshop/docs/workshop/Challenge-3-and-4/knowledge_mining_api.ipynbL65-R87](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL65-R87)`)
* Added truncation of SQL query results to a maximum of 20,000 characters to prevent excessive output. (`[microhack_workshop/docs/workshop/Challenge-3-and-4/knowledge_mining_api.ipynbL220-R308](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL220-R308)`)

### Notebook Metadata Updates
* Removed unnecessary `vscode` metadata entries from notebook cells and added a `kernelspec` configuration for `.venv` to specify the environment and Python version. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL7-R7)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL21-R17)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faR381-R396)`)

### Dependency Updates
* Upgraded `semantic-kernel[azure]` from version `1.28.0` to `1.29.0` and added `ipykernel==6.29.5` to the `requirements.txt` file to ensure compatibility with the updated notebook environment. (`[microhack_workshop/docs/workshop/requirements.txtL5-R9](diffhunk://#diff-eb444f1469e4dfffd7b3bfdd177de21c42acb99f0849958b94c55cd819d6528cL5-R9)`)

### Input and Output Adjustments
* Updated the list of user inputs and improved the formatting of output responses for better readability during execution. (`[microhack_workshop/docs/workshop/Challenge-3-and-4/knowledge_mining_api.ipynbL360-R368](diffhunk://#diff-892c07e2878ee5d8aa99f6f50d6338bb4b86888b60ed3467889f8b362c8e15faL360-R368)`)

## Overview

This PR addresses task #3 from the v0.4 Roadmap (issue #501): "Improve the chat history component".

## Implementation Details

- Added paginated chat history with infinite scroll:
  - Created new `getChatsPage` server action that supports pagination with limit/offset
  - Implemented `/api/chats` endpoint to fetch pages of chat history
  - Refactored sidebar history into server wrapper + client component architecture
  - Added intersection observer to detect scroll position and load more items
  - Added effect to synchronize props to state when new chats are created
  
- Improvements:
  - Initial load limited to 20 chats (vs. all chats previously)
  - Infinite scroll automatically loads next 20 chats when user scrolls to bottom
  - Memory usage is optimized by loading only what's needed
  - Fixes issue with new chats not appearing in history until manual refresh

## Testing

- Confirmed smooth loading of initial and subsequent chat pages
- Verified chat history updates properly when new chats are created
- Tested with large chat history to ensure performance remains good
- Validated mobile and desktop scrolling behavior

Related issue: #501 (partial)
