### Questions ?
Please refer to the [Backport tool documentation](https://github.com/sorenlouv/backport)

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Karen Grigoryan","email":"karen.grigoryan@elastic.co"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2025-05-05T09:34:23Z","message":"[Security Solution][Explore][Overview Dashboard] Move from viz responses to viz tables (#214888)

Addresses #214733

This PR revamps the visualization response handling. In most of the
affected files `useVisualizationResponse` was purely used to obtain
total count of docs to just verify if data exists. But to support that
we had to juggle with response type which is not easy to determine and
is too blanket. Unfortunately the type being too generic led to a couple
of issues described in the above mentioned ticket.

I initially tried to improve the types but the more I digged the more I
realized that it's very hard to do because it's not us who makes the
request but the Lens and request and response is actually an
implementation detail of Lens component. We control the request
indirectly by providing [lens
attributes](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/blob/main/x-pack/solutions/security/plugins/security_solution/public/common/components/visualization_actions/lens_attributes/common/events.ts#L17).
And they define the request and affect the expected shape of response.
But since exact logic of determining the shape is hidden in Lens we
cannot rely on it and cannot narrow it down with generics on our side.

So turns out Lens also exposes another object `TablesAdapter.tables`
that contains tabular data and meta data about the request and response.
From there we can access the total count of each lens response. And its
structure is more mappable to lens attributes structure. Though it has
its own nuancing and legacy deviations.

Still this is a more idiomatic way of accessing lens total counts atm.

This pull request introduces functionality for managing menu items (adding and deleting), improves error handling and loading states in various hooks, and updates the UI and translations to support these changes. Below is a summary of the most significant changes:

### New Features for Menu Management:
* Added a new `AddToMenu` view and corresponding route (`addtomenu`) in `src/App.jsx` for adding menu items. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d274a54187c91ba0f532df2a9e194e27ab50e988f5e4c33f5a7893918320c661R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d274a54187c91ba0f532df2a9e194e27ab50e988f5e4c33f5a7893918320c661R70)
* Created a new `usePostItem` hook to handle posting and deleting menu items via API calls.

### Enhancements to Hooks:
* Updated `useForm` hook to support dynamic language-specific input changes (`handleInputChangeMenu`) and improved reset functionality. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4f0d9541046a540ece0c196bacd7308584d56131d7af5ed836629a21a40dbd3bL5-L27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4f0d9541046a540ece0c196bacd7308584d56131d7af5ed836629a21a40dbd3bL43-R53) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4f0d9541046a540ece0c196bacd7308584d56131d7af5ed836629a21a40dbd3bR83-R84)
* Enhanced `useAllergens` hook with a loading state and error handling.
* Modified `useImage` to use a configurable base URL for image paths.

### UI and Styling Updates:
* Updated navigation links in `AdminBar` to include "Add to Menu" and renamed "Edit Menu" to "Delete From Menu."
* Added new CSS classes for admin filters, delete buttons, and checkbox groups in `src/style/admin.css`.
* Improved disabled button styling in `src/style/reusable-components.css`.

### Translations:
* Added new keys to `en.json` and `fi.json` for the "Add to Menu" and "Delete From Menu" pages, including form fields, validation messages, and success notifications. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f420468eb712a68d53557a4f5272b25a83938166b073c7ce47e0de8bd32064d7L183-R217) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8d27a5c0a0e302631929d404f3c62e75d0fed492ea78ff0d10351dc9cccf620bL180-R213)

### Other Improvements:

author: vampire
body:
I would like to see your action first-class supported by https://github.com/typesafegithub/github-workflows-kt, a Kotlin DSL to write GitHub Action workflows.

The project came up with ways to reduce operational load when keeping the library's action wrappers in sync with actions' inputs and outputs.
The solutions include onboarding https://github.com/typesafegithub/github-actions-typing.
It is as easy as adding an extra YAML file to your repository root, and (optionally) adding a simple GitHub workflow that validates this new file.
Thanks to this, the code generator in the Kotlin DSL can fetch typing info provided by you instead of them, which has a number of benefits.
It has no negative effects on current action consumers, they continue to use the action via regular GitHub API, as if the file was not there.

In this pull request, I would like to ask you if you are open to introduce such typings in your action and also provide the current state as far as I could determine it.
You would not be the first, there are already other actions using it, like e.g. my https://github.com/Vampire/setup-wsl or also Microsoft's https://github.com/microsoft/setup-msbuild.

Also "regular" users can benefit from this clear and formalized typing definition, seeing exactly what values are valid.
And as the typings are made independent from the Kotlin DSL library, also other DSL or similar consumers could use these typings in the future.

When accepting this PR and in the future maintaining the typing yourself,
please keep in mind that API are generated from these typing information.
So if you for example recognize that a type is wrong and want to change it for example from `string` to `integer`,
this would be a breaking change for such consumers and should therefore be done with a major version bump.
Backwards compatible changes like new enum options, or new inputs or outputs can of course be released in a minor version as usual.

After hopefully merging this PR it would be nice if you could cut a release soon,
so that the shiny new typings can be used right away.

body:
This PR:
* Disallows empty bodies. Empty body can be a result of redaction spilling over from headers and it can cover actual body. It's safer to expect the server to always return valid JSON.
* Disallows any redaction in body unless explicitly enabled. Enabling is unsafe and we'll describe in the docs - how to do it safely
* Adds a bunch of tests

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

- **New Features**
  - Introduced configurable modes for URL testing and body redaction, allowing users to select between full or prefix URL matching and enable or disable unsafe body redaction.
  - Added a new configuration structure to manage these options.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved error handling for unsafe redacted elements in response bodies, providing clearer error messages.

- **Refactor**
  - Enhanced internal equality checks and validation logic for redaction modes, resulting in stricter and more reliable verification.

author: jdevlieghere
body:
Currently, we are only using the executable name when attaching. The AttachRequestHandler isn't setting the path in the attach info, which means that we rely on the target when attaching by name. When wo go down this path, we only look at the executable's filename, not its full path. Since we know the full path from the attach arguments, we should specify it in the attach info.

Fixes #138197

author: cristianoventura
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description

Some users have faced issues where k6 Studio proxy can't reach their network (because of a proxy misconfiguration or upstream issue with a corporate network). This makes network requests fail without telling the user what the problem is.

This PR implements health checks right after k6 Studio proxy launches. Using the current proxy configuration the user has, the proxy will attempt to connect to the internet, and the status will change to "Unhealthy" upon failure.

<!-- A short (or detailed) description of what this PR does and why these changes are needed -->

## How to Test

There are a couple of ways to reproduce the healthy and unhealthy status of the proxy.

<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes -->

## Replicate a healthy proxy

### Option 1. Launch the proxy in regular mode

This should always return healthy, unless internet connection can't be established.

### Option 2. Connect to upstream instance of mitmproxy _with a valid certificate_

- In k6 Studio working directory, launch a new instance of mitmproxy. It's important that the `confdir` parameter points to the `certificates` folder.

```sh
mitmdump --mode regular@7005 --set confdir=./resources/certificates
```

- In k6 Studio, change proxy mode to "upstream"
- Set "Server URL" to `localhost:7005` (or the port you launched mitmdump)
- Set "Certificate path" to the `mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem` located in the `./resources/certificates` folder
- You can also unset the certificate path but check "Skip SSL verification"


## Replicate an unhealthy proxy

### Option 1. Specify a nonexistent upstream address

- In k6 Studio, change proxy mode to "upstream"
- Set "Server URL" to an address that doesn't exist (e.g. `localhost:9999`)

### Option 2. Connect to upstream instance of mitmproxy _without a certificate_

- In k6 Studio working directory, launch a new instance of mitmproxy. It's important that the `confdir` parameter points to the existing `certificates` folder.

```sh
mitmdump --mode regular@7005 --set confdir=./resources/certificates
```

- In k6 Studio, change proxy mode to "upstream"
- Set "Server URL" to `localhost:7005` (or the port you launched mitmdump)
- Do not set "Certificate path"
- Do not check "Skip SSL verification"

author: mergify[bot]
body:
There were a few issues:
1. BUG: `rabbitmqctl export definitions -` would export the `default_queue_type` within vhost's metadata if set explicitly (correct) but also outside of the `metadata` block even if not set explicitly for the vhost (not correct)
2. BUG/consistency issue: HTTP API / `rabbitmqadmin` would always export the default queue type in both places
- outside of the `metadata` block is just redundant
- inside the `metadata` block is inconsistent with `rabbitmqctl export_definitions` (the difference stems from the fact that CTL only exports existing vhosts' metadata, while HTTP API injects the configuration-level DQT into each vhost's `metadata` upon export)
3. The aforementioned inject-upon-export logic is prone to confusion: I can have a system with no DQT configuration and export definitions from it, then restart with a DQT on the node configuration level and export again. The exports will be different because the configuration-level default changed and the current default is injected into the export.

This PR changes the DQT logic: no DQT is injected upon export because it's injected/inherited from the node's configuration into vhost's metadata when a vhost is declared. Therefore each vhost has its own DQT explicitly defined and it's always present in any export (both CTL and HTTP API).

The downsides of this approach is that export/import between systems with a different configuration-level DQT will now require adjusting the DQT in the JSON file

However the logic is should be easier now and more consistent with how queue-level DQT works: when a queue is declared without a type, the default queue type is injected. Going forward, DQT changes don't affect the queue. Similarly, now if a vhost with no DQT is declared, configuration-level DQT is injected and configuration changes don't affect existing vhosts.<hr>This is an automatic backport of pull request #13837 done by [Mergify](https://mergify.com).

body:
This pull request adds two new Jupyter notebooks, `21_stack_unstack.ipynb` and `22_pivot.ipynb`, to demonstrate data transformation techniques using pandas. The notebooks focus on reshaping datasets with `stack` and `unstack` methods and creating pivot tables for data analysis, respectively.

### New Notebooks for Data Transformation and Analysis:

#### Notebook on `stack` and `unstack`:
* Introduced a step-by-step guide in `notebooks/21_stack_unstack.ipynb` to demonstrate reshaping data using pandas' `stack` and `unstack` methods. The notebook includes importing libraries, loading a dataset, reshaping data, and cleaning column names for clarity.

#### Notebook on Pivot Tables:
* Added `notebooks/22_pivot.ipynb` to illustrate the creation and use of pivot tables in pandas. This notebook covers reshaping data, renaming columns, and generating pivot tables with grouping and aggregation functions for summarizing data.

## 🗒️ What

<!--
Briefly list out the changes proposed in this PR.
-->
Set a configurable char limit on broken link reports.

## 🤷 Why

<!--
Describe why the changes proposed are needed. Some examples: new feature requested, refactor to make things easier later, styling tweaks requested by design, etc.
-->
 This is to avoid a limitation in the GH API preventing the creation of a PR comment with a body longer than 65536 characters. Attempting to do so (as can happen when there are a lot of broken links) produces the following error:

```
Error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"IssueComment","code":"unprocessable","field":"data","message":"Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)"}
```

## 🛠️ How

<!--
Dive into the approach you took, list resources you referenced, detail other approaches you tried but didn't end up going with, etc.
-->

## 🧪 Testing


<!--
Create a checklist for going through how to test your proposed changes. If there is anything to configure before interacting with the project in a browser, such as toggling feature flags, changing machine settings, or simulating behavior in browser dev tools, list those steps first.

- [ ] Step 1
- [ ] Step 2
- [ ] Step 3
- [ ] ...
-->

[A PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/web-unified-docs/pull/387) has been opened against this branch (`rm/lychee-results-to-gh-artifacts`) to test this without merging into `main`. That PR has a large number of files changed and the links intentionally broken, so that the char length of the report exceeds the maximum char limit(configurable as a variable [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/web-unified-docs/settings/variables/actions)). Looking at that PR, we can see that the full report has been uploaded to GH artifacts and a link posted as a PR comment instead

author: rauks
body:
Hi,
Many thanks for your work again! 😄

This PR aims to fix the ordering of the LoRAs, Recipes and Checkpoints when sorted by names.

Currently, the ordering is performed using the `sorted` method, which orders items lexicographically:

- Model 10
- Model 11
- Model 8
- Model 9

![unsorted wall](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c9f4b92-4694-437d-91be-f87678dda652)

![api unsorted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be24d231-d0f1-4a1e-b65f-2562ce4fa7c1)

The proposal is to use a [natural ordering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_sort_order) instead:

- Adding a dependency to the `natsort` module.
  - https://pypi.org/project/natsort
  - https://github.com/SethMMorton/natsort
- Using `natsorted` instead of `sorted` when ordering by name (drop-in replacement).

Changing the sort to:

- Model 8
- Model 9
- Model 10
- Model 11

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf9355f1-4f3f-4dd8-b407-e86194c48360)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6828f290-8c78-4023-b0a3-60a8386dc1a1)

This works with more complex cases such as below (natural order on the types and versions):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edb435cd-c7d8-4a7a-920d-4d75fdb72b21)

author: abrodriguezalman
body:
We want to add functionality to allow a user to DELETE a review for a game.

I have implemented an API Endpoint that deals with handling DELETE and PATCH requests for Reviews using the existing Review object and serializer. More specifically, I created a Review Detail View that allows a user to see the details of a review, patch or delete a review. The View also ensures that only the original author of the review is able to delete it or patch it, otherwise a permission error is raised.

To test this functionality, visit a URL of the format http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/games/<int:game_id>/reviews/create/ and create a review as a logged in user. Then, visit http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/games/<int:game_id>/reviews/<int:pk>/  where pk is the id of your review (you should be able to see this id on the /reviews/ page). You should be able to see details of the review (given that such review exists), as well as delete/patch the review. 

To test that review owners can delete/patch their reviews, follow the previous steps to create a sample review as a logged in user. Then, log out and try to access the detail page of your review again. You should get an error whenever you try to delete or patch the review.

body: **PR part of Fix-It Week 2025** In this PR, we add a new section to the ReadTheDocs sidebar: the "Developer Guides". The Developer Guides section is meant to hold tutorials to help developers build code with SIMSOPT's features. As the first tutorial in the developer guides we added the "Using the Derivative class" tutorial, which teaches developers how to build an objective function with derivatives in SIMSOPT. Learning how to add derivatives to Optimizable objects has been a challenge for many developers, in our experience. Attached are two screenshots showing the new entry in the sidebar and the tutorial. \ \ **Tests** No tests are needed since this is a documentation fix.

author: hasith12345
body:
This pull request introduces significant changes to the inventory and shop management functionality in both the backend and frontend. The changes include refactoring the `Shop` model to consolidate categories within the shop schema, updating API endpoints for adding and removing products, and improving the frontend to support toggling products in and out of the shop. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Backend Refactoring and Enhancements

* **Refactored `Shop` model**: Merged the `Category` schema into the `Shop` schema, allowing categories to be nested directly within the shop. This simplifies the data structure and removes the need for a separate `Category` model. The `Shop` schema now includes `categories` as an array of objects, each containing a name and associated products. (`[Backend/models/Shop.jsL21-L67](diffhunk://#diff-7208365d3756edbe95ff4e216049876087ca9a64aa8d063dd56cb64b16aa2a14L21-L67)`)
* **Updated product management in shop**: Refactored logic for adding and removing products from shop categories. The new implementation directly manipulates the `categories` array in the `Shop` model, eliminating the need to save separate `Category` documents. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d0bb2f367dd77c19f5270a2106765412fb9d87a92f07cb8277d7a73d4fafab34L168-R191)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d0bb2f367dd77c19f5270a2106765412fb9d87a92f07cb8277d7a73d4fafab34L207-R230)`)
* **Improved API endpoints**:
  - Added a new `removeProductFromShop` endpoint to handle product removal with query parameters for `salonId` and `category`. (`[Backend/routes/inventoryRoutes.jsL36-R43](diffhunk://#diff-420ffcc614f05d7ff260bea717591023a9ce3294bb49bb5848692f0c5cf246ffL36-R43)`)
  - Updated `getProductsByCategory` to validate the category and return products directly from the populated `categories` field in the `Shop` model. (`[Backend/controllers/shopController.jsL90-R113](diffhunk://#diff-17cbf208dd19155ca3c28dfe54f1c6debea8f7b13a11b512fe021cefbb56ee50L90-R113)`)

### Frontend Updates

* **Enhanced product toggle functionality**: Updated the `ProductDetailsDialog` and `InventoryPage` components to support toggling products in and out of the shop. The `handleAddToShop` function now determines whether to add or remove a product based on its current state. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b21ae824628fc1864ebb3e34a4c3f039f193e25befc7c8449023201f97ad3618L211-R211)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-22152b5d78b9680bb73a32b1ba88c3391b346ef00b0866100099ec01ce882afdL247-R285)`)
* **Improved routing and UI**:
  - Replaced the `Products` component with `ProductsPage` for better naming consistency. (`[Frontend/SalonApplication/src/App.tsxL38-R38](diffhunk://#diff-d903b15c844ba036d25b946de52f8facc50e2ac1fd6707195233c8a77e28a753L38-R38)`)
  - Updated routes in `App.tsx` to include the new `ProductsPage` and ensure proper navigation for shop-related pages. (`[Frontend/SalonApplication/src/App.tsxL63-R91](diffhunk://#diff-d903b15c844ba036d25b946de52f8facc50e2ac1fd6707195233c8a77e28a753L63-R91)`)

### Cleanup and Optimization

* **Removed unused `console.log` statements**: Cleaned up debugging logs from the backend controllers to improve code readability. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d0bb2f367dd77c19f5270a2106765412fb9d87a92f07cb8277d7a73d4fafab34L20-L24)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d0bb2f367dd77c19f5270a2106765412fb9d87a92f07cb8277d7a73d4fafab34L63-L64)`)
* **Deleted redundant endpoints**: Removed the `getCategories` endpoint, which previously returned all unique categories across shops, as it is no longer needed with the new schema. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-17cbf208dd19155ca3c28dfe54f1c6debea8f7b13a11b512fe021cefbb56ee50L21-L40)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c4711c630896906ae7207647093e8708057bcdc766ea5aaa0b47ea52a9b4ce9bL8-R12)`)

author: iskettaneh
body: The first 2 commits are based on https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/146085 This PR reduces the replica mutex contention for both checkExecutionCanProceedBeforeStorageSnapshot and checkExecutionCanProceedAfterStorageSnapshot by making each of the two methods only briefly take the mutex and release it after it copies everything it needs. Running this microbenchmark: ``` rm -f /tmp/*.pb.gz && env GODEBUG=runtimecontentionstacks=1 go test ./pkg/sql/tests -run - -bench BenchmarkParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write -v -test.benchtime=3000x -test.outputdir=/tmp -test.mutexprofile=mutex.pb.gz -test.mutexprofilefraction=100 -test.timeout 25s 2>&1 ``` shows that the ReplicaMutex contention goes from `786.9ms` to `614.3ms`. Before: After: Running benchdiff command: ``` rm -f /tmp/*.pb.gz && env GODEBUG=runtimecontentionstacks=1 benchdiff -b --old 6cbfc38325b68a2547165ef194699c781b15f476 -c 20 ./pkg/sql/tests -r BenchmarkParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write --mutexprofile -d=3000x ``` Shows the resutls: ``` name old time/op new time/op delta ParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write-24 1.39ms ± 4% 1.39ms ± 3% ~ (p=0.912 n=10+10) name old errs/op new errs/op delta ParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write-24 0.01 ±57% 0.01 ±27% ~ (p=0.092 n=10+10) name old alloc/op new alloc/op delta ParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write-24 2.07MB ± 1% 2.07MB ± 1% ~ (p=0.912 n=10+10) name old allocs/op new allocs/op delta ParallelSysbench/SQL/3node/oltp_read_write-24 8.29k ± 1% 8.30k ± 1% ~ (p=0.684 n=10+10) ``` References: #140235 Release note: None

author: felixrieseberg
body:
We previously had a placeholder for `AbortSignals` in the API, but since those cannot be sent across process boundaries, I had to come with an alternative. I first tried having the end developer pass an `AbortSignal` to our preload script, which we could then turn into UUID before turning it back into an `AbortSignal` right before we pass it to `node-llama-cpp` - but since `AbortSignals` don't even make it into the isolated context of the preload script, I decided to go with something much simpler. Developers can now pass in a `requestUUID` into their calls - and if they do, they can abort a running operation by calling an API.

Since we're still in an experimental phase here, I don't think we should bump major.

# Remove Trino Prometheus Scrape Config

## Type of change
- [ ] Work behind a feature flag
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Improvement
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor (code improvement with no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test update

## Description

### Product
- Removing Trino scrape config for Prometheus. An error was blocking all metrics collection. Trino did not have a dashboard or documentation for their metrics and metrics will also roll off after some time so collecting them was of no value to the end user.

### Technical
- Removes Trino scrape config from Prometheus
- Issue with sharding (below), which is not used in our Prometheus setup. [Sharding is used by the prometheus-operator](https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/blob/main/Documentation/user-guides/shards-and-replicas.md). 
- Prometheus was unable to parse the scrape config and this was blocking all metric collection. But this had been working on big-02 and it is unclear why it is not working on tag-big-01. There are no dashboards and [limited documentation on Trino metrics](https://trino.io/docs/current/admin/openmetrics.html#coordinator-and-worker-metrics-with-kubernetes). Considering it's causing an error in production and adding no value we think it is better to remove.

Prometheus server error message.
```
time=2025-05-05T18:00:57.665Z level=ERROR source=main.go:597 msg="Error loading config (--config.file=/etc/config/prometheus.yml)" file=/etc/config/prometheus.yml err="parsing YAML file /etc/config/prometheus.yml: yaml: unmarshal errors:\n  line 376: cannot unmarshal !!str `$(SHARDS)` into uint64\n  line 421: cannot unmarshal !!str `$(SHARDS)` into uint64"
```

## Impact

### Security 

##### Authorization
N/A

##### Appsec
N/A

### Performance
N/A

### Data
N/A

### Backward compatibility
Removing a scrape config should not be an issue. Metrics will no longer be collected and will drop out of Prometheus eventually.

Tested on big-02.

N/A

author: ebsmothers
body:
Separating out our async RL tests into their own runner, which runs only under certain conditions.

We now have two GPU jobs:

`rl_test.yaml` runs only if any of the `dev/rl` or `dev/grpo` files are modified. It will run only our async RL tests, which now need to be decorated by `@rl_test()`. The YAML file currently assumes that any such tests live under `tests/recipes/dev/rl` or `tests/torchtune/dev/rl`. If we move our async RL tests or add any in a new location we will need to update the runner's pytest command to include them.

`gpu_test.yaml` runs all other tests (i.e. our full test suite prior to #2637) on every PR. 

For local pytest runs, async RL tests will be skipped by default. Any pytest command can be supplemented with the flag `--run-rl-tests` in order to run them. (Note that RL tests are a subset of integration tests, so you will also need to use either `-m integration_test` or `--with-integration` as well.)

   - 유저별, 일간, 주간, 월간, 학과별 랭킹을 제공하는 새로운 페이지를 추가.
   - 탭별 전환을 통해 필터링된 데이터를 보여주며, 등수에 따라 금/은/동 색상 및 아이콘 표시.
   - 배경 로고 이미지와 반투명 배경 등 시각적 요소를 활용하여 디자인 완성도 향상.

3. **PDF 업로드 모달 추가 (`PdfUploadModal.jsx`)**
   - 드래그 앤 드롭 또는 버튼 클릭을 통한 PDF 파일 업로드 기능 제공.
   - 비 PDF 형식 업로드 시 경고 메시지 출력.
   - 컴포넌트화하여 재사용 가능하게 설계.

4. **기존 컴포넌트 스타일 개선**
   - `SelectableButton.jsx`, `Dropdown.jsx`의 스타일에 `hover`, `focus`, `bg-white` 속성 추가로 시각적 일관성 강화.

5. **라우터 등록 및 이미지 최적화**
   - `App.jsx`에서 `/ranking` 경로를 등록하여 신규 페이지 접근 가능.
   - 사용하지 않는 이미지(`hero-slogan.png`, `sub-slogan.png`, `sub-description.png`) 삭제.
   - 새로운 로고 이미지(`image-logo-background.png`) 추가.

6. **Tailwind 설정 확장 (`tailwind.config.js`)**
   - 색상(`lightbrown`, `brown`, `darkbrown`)과 폰트(`Namdhinggo`)를 사용자 정의 설정에 추가하여 프로젝트 전반에서 통일된 스타일링 가능.

author: bolinfest
body:
This adds initial support for MCP servers in the style of Claude Desktop and Cursor. Note this PR is the bare minimum to get things working end to end: all configured MCP servers are launched every time Codex is run, there is no recovery for MCP servers that crash, etc.

(Also, I took some shortcuts to change some fields of `Session` to be `pub(crate)`, which also means there are circular deps between `codex.rs` and `mcp_tool_call.rs`, but I will clean that up in a subsequent PR.)

`codex-rs/README.md` is updated as part of this PR to explain how to use this feature. There is a bit of plumbing to route the new settings from `Config` to the business logic in `codex.rs`. The most significant chunks for new code are in `mcp_connection_manager.rs` (which defines the `McpConnectionManager` struct) and `mcp_tool_call.rs`, which is responsible for tool calls.

This PR also introduces new `McpToolCallBegin` and `McpToolCallEnd` event types to the protocol, but does not add any handlers for them. (See https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/836 for initial usage.)

To test, I added the following to my `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
# Local build of https://github.com/hideya/mcp-server-weather-js
[mcp_servers.weather]
command = "/Users/mbolin/code/mcp-server-weather-js/dist/index.js"
args = []
```

And then I ran the following:

```
codex-rs$ cargo run --bin codex exec 'what is the weather in san francisco'
[2025-05-06T22:40:05] Task started: 1
[2025-05-06T22:40:18] Agent message: Here’s the latest National Weather Service forecast for San Francisco (downtown, near 37.77° N, 122.42° W):

This Afternoon (Tue):
• Sunny, high near 69 °F
• West-southwest wind around 12 mph

Tonight:
• Partly cloudy, low around 52 °F
• SW wind 7–10 mph
...
```

Note that Codex itself is not able to make network calls, so it would not normally be able to get live weather information like this. However, the weather MCP is [currently] not run under the Codex sandbox, so it is able to hit `api.weather.gov` and fetch current weather information.

author: scottypoi
body:
Fix for ContentLookup bug described in #711 

Concurrent requets should be limited to 5, however, we were often seeing logs like: 
```
7e7fd:Portal:BeaconNetwork:LOOKUP:0x10f090… Have 19 peers left to ask and 10 pending requests
```

This happened because any time a peer request returned (without content), it would trigger the next recursive round of requets, which would add 5 new requests to the batch.

However, we do want to avoid the need to wait for full batches of 5 to complete before continuing the recursive search.

The solution is to check the number of pending requests before adding more to the batch, and to limit the total number of requests in the new batch and old to 5.  We accomplish this with this line:
```
        const peerBatch: LookupPeer[] = []
        const availableSlots = 5 - this.pending.size
        while (this.lookupPeers.peek() && peerBatch.length < availableSlots) {
          const next = this.lookupPeers.pop()!
          peerBatch.push(next)
        }
```

----

This solution did limit the total pending requests to 5, but did not solve another underlying issue of incomplete requests hanging open.  Because of this, we will simply end up with a set of 5 pending requests that never close.

To solve this, we couple each request with an `abortPromise` using [`AbortController`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController), and `AbortSignal`.  The promise will reject when the signal is aborted.  The actual content request is raced against this abort promise.  If the signal is aborted, the request is cancelled and cleaned up, and the pending request is removed from the tracking set.  

This seems to solve the hanging request issue, which should also solve some memory leaks and resource exhaustion issues.

author: parthosa
body:
Fixes #1662

## Issue

In Bootstrap (Qual AutoTuner), all GPU-related configs are shown even when unchanged, misleading users into thinking they are AutoTuner recommendations. For instance, it may carry over CPU configs like `spark.executor.memory` even when the system lacks sufficient memory for RAPIDS plugin. See issue description for complete example.

## Improvements
This PR fixes the issue by recommending `[FILL_IN_VALUE]` for memory-related configurations when available memory is insufficient, rather than carrying forward CPU run values.

### Before:
```
--conf spark.executor.cores=16
--conf spark.executor.memory=12000m
--conf spark.rapids.memory.pinnedPool.size=1g
```

### After:
```
Spark Properties:
--conf spark.executor.cores=16
--conf spark.executor.memory=[FILL_IN_VALUE]
--conf spark.rapids.memory.pinnedPool.size=[FILL_IN_VALUE]

Comments:
- This node/worker configuration is not ideal for using the RAPIDS Accelerator
  for Apache Spark because it doesn't have enough memory for the executors.
  We recommend using nodes/workers with more memory. Need at least 42188 MB
  memory per executor.
```

## Code Changes
- Updated `com.nvidia.spark.rapids.tool.tuning.AutoTuner#calcOverallMemory()`
        - Introduced logic to apply default values (instead of minimums) for memory overheads which are more practical recommendations.
        - Simplified the logic to detect when memory is insufficient and added a warning comment indicating that the current setup is suboptimal.


## Test
- Added two unit tests in QualificationAutoTunerSuite when:
   1. Less memory available for executors
   2. Sufficient memory available for executors (use the value recommended by AutoTuner)

- Integrated existing `auth` module into the `clients` module.
- Applied `JwtAuthGuard` to protect client routes with authentication.

## Changes
- Imported `JwtAuthGuard` in the clients controller.
- Now only authenticated users can access the client endpoints.

## How to test
1. Start the application and generate a valid JWT token using the login route.
2. Make a request to any client route **with** the token in the `Authorization` header (e.g., `Bearer <token>`).
3. Confirm the request is successful.
4. Try the same request **without** a token and confirm it returns `401 Unauthorized`.

## Notes
- This PR **does not** modify the auth module itself.
- Only integrates and applies the guard in the clients feature.

author: jslair
body:
## 🧩 Summary

This pull request combines two major updates:

1. **Seda 2.3 Compatibility and Structural Refactoring**  
2. **Massive Enhancements to Mail Extraction Capabilities**

Both initiatives aim to improve performance, maintainability, standards compliance, and overall robustness across the system.

---

## 📁 Seda 2.3 Support & Metadata Refactoring

- Introduced **Seda 2.3 support** across data models, editors, and validation tools.
- Created a unified `AbstractUnitaryDataObject` shared by `BinaryDataObject` and `PhysicalDataObject`, centralizing logic and reducing redundancy.
- Refactored metadata handling using `ComplexListInterface` to support flexible and dynamic Seda 2.3 metadata.
- Enhanced GUI editors (`BinaryDataObjectEditor`, `PhysicalDataObjectEditor`) to support new metadata types and user-friendly interaction.
- Replaced outdated `DescriptionLevel` with a unified `EnumType`.

### 🔧 Key Changes

- Support for complex metadata structures and validation for Seda 2.3.
- Consolidation of list and map types for better implementation efficiency.
- Improved modularity and testability across affected components.
- Seda 2.3 validation enabled in all tools.

---

## 📨 Mail Extraction Overhaul

- **Full refactor** of the mail extraction engine with major performance boost (2–3× faster on 4-core systems).
- Support for **signed emails** (PKCS#7, PGP).
- Improved extraction of metadata: sender, recipients, subject, date, attachments, plain/text content, etc.
- Fixed MIME parsing for Thunderbird/mbox/eml formats (previously broken).
- Better handling of exotic encodings (e.g., tolerant UTF decoding, UTF-7 support).
- Extended command-line and parameter flexibility.

### 🌍 UI Enhancements

- Internationalized the `MailExtract` UI (now supports English).
- Better CLI syntax and full parameter exposure.
- Improved log display with overload protection (while full logs still saved to disk).

---

## 🧪 Testing & Validation

- Improved cross-platform test builds.
- Increased unit and integration test coverage.
- New test cases for complex or malformed emails.
- Seda 2.3 support thoroughly tested.
- Updated dependencies (e.g., Droid with Java 17 support).

---

## 🧹 Code Cleanup & Dependency Updates

- Deprecated code and unused dependencies removed.
- Integrated `java-libpst` as a Maven module with thread-safety fixes.
- Migrated to **Java 17** as the minimum JVM version (required by newer libraries like Apache Tika).

---

## 📚 Documentation

- Updated README with new mail features and usage.
- Technical comments and inline documentation improved throughout.

---

## ✅ Impact

- Full Seda 2.3 compatibility with more maintainable and scalable code structure.
- Email extraction is now faster, more reliable, and standards-compliant.
- Codebase is cleaner, better documented, and modernized (Java 17).
- UI and CLI improvements contribute to a better developer and user experience.

---

## 🔧 To Do (Post-Merge)

- Enhance `Compact/Decompact` functions to support all SEDA versions.
- Clarify and finalize disk export strategies (`ObjectDataVersion` vs `ObjectDataUse/ObjectDataNumber`) for `mailextractlib` and `sedalib`.

author: ceski-1
body:
Fixes https://github.com/fabiangreffrath/woof/issues/2105

This limits the volume when a large number of channels are playing the same sound. For simplicity, this feature is toggled using the existing "Output Limiter" menu option (which also toggles OpenAL Soft's built-in limiter). There are two new config-only settings: `snd_channels_per_sfx` and `snd_volume_per_sfx`. The defaults seem balanced to me.

How it works:
1. A new sound is about to start.
2. If there are too many channels playing the sound, then stop the lowest priority channel. If none are lower, don't start the new sound.
3. If the total volume of all channels playing the sound is too loud, then reduce the volume of each of those channels.

Testing:
1. Set "Sound Volume" to 1 for easier comparisons
2. Toggle "Output Limiter" on or off
3. Test wads:
    a. [dsda_parallellimit.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20050755/dsda_parallellimit.zip)
    b. [lifts_and_stairs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20050758/lifts_and_stairs.zip)
    c. [scythe](https://www.doomworld.com/idgames/levels/doom2/megawads/scythe) (map26)
    d. Default plasma and [nice_plasma.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20050760/nice_plasma.zip)
    e. The above plus [bunch_of_spiders.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20051056/bunch_of_spiders.zip)

Sounds okay to me, but I recommend some testing and feedback from users.
